chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz al-Kufi from Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb from Ja'far from his father, peace be upon them both:

That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman whose husband died, when the news reached her and her waiting period (iddah) had expired, the mourning (iddah) is obligatory upon her. He said: 'If the news does not reach her until her waiting period expires, then all of that is gone, and she may marry whomever she wishes.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: A woman whose husband has died

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a widow's waiting period if she learns of her husband's death after her iddah has already expired?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the widow's waiting period (iddah) is tied to the actual occurrence of death rather than the notification, meaning if the iddah elapses before she learns of the death, her mourning obligation is fully discharged. This ruling, transmitted through the Kufi scholar al-Sindi, underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal obligations are contingent upon the actual event, providing practical ease for widows in pre-modern contexts where news delays were common. It distinguishes between the ritual mourning (hidad) and the legal prohibition of marriage (iddah), allowing immediate remarriage once the latter is complete.
